items.claim: The unit's observed_substrate_signals field names a koh-amar formula that does not occur anywhere within Jer.13.20-13.27, while the seam at 13:20 and the judgment_oracle typing are both byte-sound.
items.evidence: A consonantal sweep for koh amar returns the book's full 153-verse total, with chapter 13's total of four sites (sweep: 4 verses) exhausted at 13:1, 13:9, 13:12, and 13:13, all preceding this span, leaving the stretch from 13:20 through 13:27 with a zero count, so the koh_amar entry in the signal list is not supported by the span's own bytes. The span's actual divine-formula token is the neum-YHWH closure marker נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.13.25, byte tier), rendering “says Yahweh” (web:Jer.13.25) -- closure corroboration, a different formula from koh-amar. Independently, the addressee shift the seam rests on is real: 13:18's crowned pair carries plural suffixes (מַרְאֲשׁ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם, תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם, oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier), while 13:20 onward carries singular-feminine suffixes throughout, starting with תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), closing on the explicit Jerusalem vocative at 13:27; and the closing apostrophe uses the distinct oy lexeme (sweep: 8 verses book-wide), not the vav-prefixed hoy of the woe oracles, so judgment_oracle rather than woe_oracle is the right call. The defect is confined to the mislabeled signal.
tier_citations: consonantal sweep: koh amar = 153 verses book-wide, ch.13 sites at 13:1/13:9/13:12/13:13 only

items.claim: The header-plus-description bundling at Jer.14.1-14.6 and its judgment_oracle typing both hold up against the bytes.
items.evidence: The asher-hayah debar-YHWH el-Yirmeyahu header at 14:1 is one of four attested sites for this shape book-wide (sweep: 4 verses: 14:1, 46:1, 47:1, 49:34); no addressee or scene shift separates it from the drought description running through 14:6, matching how the shape's other sites carry their attached content as one unit. The petuchah at 13:27 and the absence of any parashah mark inside 14:1-14:6 are both accurately disclosed.
tier_citations: consonantal sweep: asher-hayah debar-YHWH el-Yirmeyahu = 4 verses book-wide

items.claim: The seam at 14:7 and the lament_confession typing both match the bytes: a first-person-plural plea to Yahweh opens where the third-person drought report ends, and this span is a named communal-lament instance in the closed vocabulary.
items.evidence: 14:7 opens אִם עֲוֺנֵ֨ינוּ֙ עָ֣נוּ (oshb:Jer.14.7, byte tier), a first-person-plural voice addressed to Yahweh that is absent from the preceding third-person description; the plea continues through 14:8 to a setumah-marked close at 14:9.

items.claim: Isolating 14:10 as a one-verse unit is warranted by independent addressee shifts on both edges, not by the mere recurrence of koh-amar.
items.evidence: 14:10 opens כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier), a third-person pronouncement about the people, distinct from the people's own direct plea just closed and from the private “Yahweh said to me” frame that opens next at web:Jer.14.11; both flanking setumah marks are accurately disclosed, and the koh-amar-with-frame-owner-change pairing keeps the cut from being mere formula-fragmentation.

items.claim: The six-verse private dialogue is correctly kept whole because the internal koh-amar onset at 14:15 keeps the same frame-owner and addressee, so it is not a valid cutting point.
items.evidence: The span opens with the private-address frame וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.14.11, byte tier), rendering “Yahweh said to me” (web:Jer.14.11), sustained through Jeremiah's own protest at 14:13 and into Yahweh's reply. The koh-amar recurrence at 14:15, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.15, byte tier), stays inside that same reported private exchange with no new addressee, so leaving it uncut is correct: koh-amar recurring without a frame-owner change is corroboration, not a seam.

items.claim: The discourse-imperative seam at 14:17 is byte-sound, and typing the commissioned dirge as judgment_oracle rather than lament_confession is the correct closed-vocabulary call despite its mourning register.
items.evidence: 14:17 opens the command וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier), distinct from the third-person indictment of the false prophets closing at 14:16; the span is not one of the chapter's two named communal-lament units (14:7-9 and 14:19-22), so the announced-judgment content controls the typing over the weeping register.

items.claim: The seam at 14:19 and the lament_confession typing both match the bytes, and stopping the span before 15:1 correctly tracks a real addressee change.
items.evidence: 14:19 opens הֲמָאֹ֨ס מָאַ֜סְתָּ אֶת יְהוּדָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.19, byte tier), a return to first-person-plural direct address to Yahweh after the dirge closes; the plea runs to a petuchah-marked close at 14:22. The following verse (web:Jer.15.1) answers in Yahweh's voice but addresses Jeremiah rather than Yahweh's own hearers, so excluding it from this span is correct.

items.claim: The seam at 15:1 is byte-sound, the internal koh-amar at 15:2 is correctly left uncut as reported speech inside the same address frame, and the span's own close at 15:4 sits before a genuine addressee shift.
items.evidence: 15:1 opens וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.15.1, byte tier), continuing without a new addressee through the four-fold sentence and the Manasseh clause at 15:4; the koh-amar at 15:2, כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier), is words Jeremiah is told to relay within that same frame, not a fresh frame-owner. The petuchah at 14:22 and the absence of any mark inside 15:1-15:4 are disclosed, and the span's close precedes a direct Jerusalem apostrophe opening at web:Jer.15.5, confirming the endpoint against neighboring bytes.
